column3: NASB renders “on the Sabbaths” as “on the Sabbath.”
NASB renders “Ha!” as “Let us alone!” and “What to us and to You” as “What business do we have with each other.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “down” and “of the people.”
NASB renders “word” as “message” and the question “they come out?” as a statement.
NASB follows the critical text; “a great fever” is rendered “a high fever,” and “appealed for her” is “asked Him to help her.”
NASB follows the critical text (“laying … He was healing”).
NASB follows the critical text with “the Son of God” (no “the Christ”).
NASB follows the critical text and supplies “Jesus.”
NASB follows the critical text; “evangelize” is rendered “preach.”
NASB follows the critical text with “the synagogues of Judea.”
